boundary_rationale: Opens with the imperative-vocative בֵּ֖ית יַעֲקֹ֑ב לְכ֥וּ וְנֵלְכָ֖ה (oshb:Isa.2.5, byte tier), “House of Jacob, come, and let's walk in the light of Yahweh.” (web:Isa.2.5), reusing the ‘Jacob’ catchword from the preceding oracle as a hook while opening its own address. The row runs through the description of pride, idolatry, and the coming terror of Yahweh, closing on the refrain-clause וְנִשְׂגַּ֧ב יְהוָ֛ה לְבַדּ֖וֹ בַּיּ֥וֹם הַהֽוּא (oshb:Isa.2.11, byte tier), “Yahweh alone will be exalted in that day.” (web:Isa.2.11), where a setumah break is recorded (oshb:Isa.2.11, single-witness, tier-3); the row's own opening seam carries a mark too, a petuchah closing verse 4 (oshb:Isa.2.4, single-witness, tier-3) just before it. The identical clause recurs verbatim at 2:17 (byte tier, collated against both sites, sweep: 2 verses), closing a parallel second stanza and arguing that the refrain brackets each stanza rather than the whole 2:5-22 complex.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading 2:5-22 as one unbroken oracle was rejected because the closing refrain clause recurs byte-identically at 2:11 and 2:17, arguing that the refrain closes two shorter stanzas rather than leaving the whole complex uncut, on the same bracket-closing logic used for repeated refrains elsewhere in the book; the flight-from-terror motif that recurs from 2:10 into 2:19 and 2:21 (accent_stripped tier; sweep: 3 verses) does not disturb this division either, since its two later sites lie beyond the present stanza and argue only at complex level, not against this stanza's own closing bracket.

device_notes: Verse 6's second-person accusation (“you have forsaken your people, the house of Jacob”, web:Isa.2.6), נָטַ֗שְׁתָּה עַמְּךָ֙ (oshb:Isa.2.6, tokens 2-3, a 2ms perfect with a 2ms suffix), leaves its grammatical addressee ambiguous in the Hebrew; this construal question is held open and not resolved by the row. The refrain's own ‘loftiness of man’ clause varies in word order between 2:11 and 2:17 (form variant, not byte-identical); only the closing ‘Yahweh alone… in that day’ clause is byte-identical at both sites. A flight-from-terror motif crosses the row's own closing seam: the four-token core מִפְּנֵי֙ פַּ֣חַד יְהוָ֔ה וּמֵהֲדַ֖ר (oshb:Isa.2.10) recurs at oshb:Isa.2.19 and oshb:Isa.2.21, accent_stripped tier across the three sites (sweep: 3 verses); the later two share a byte-identical eight-token run (מִפְּנֵ֞י פַּ֤חַד יְהוָה֙ וּמֵהֲדַ֣ר גְּאוֹנ֔וֹ בְּקוּמ֖וֹ לַעֲרֹ֥ץ הָאָֽרֶץ, sweep: 2 verses, byte), while the earlier site's majesty noun is defective against the plene spelling at the later two. A low/bow root chain also runs through the stanza: וַיִּשְׁפַּל (oshb:Isa.2.9), וְשַׁ֖ח (oshb:Isa.2.11), וְשָׁפֵֽל (oshb:Isa.2.12), and וְשַׁח֙ (oshb:Isa.2.17), standing at 10 verses book-wide (sweep: 10 verses, skeleton).

boundary_rationale: Opens with the Day-of-Yahweh formula כִּ֣י י֞וֹם לַיהוָ֧ה צְבָא֛וֹת (oshb:Isa.2.12, byte tier), “For there will be a day of Yahweh of Armies” (web:Isa.2.12), a fresh temporal-formula onset launching the catalogue of high and lofty things (cedars, oaks, mountains, towers, ships, imagery) that closes on the same refrain clause as the preceding stanza, וְנִשְׂגַּ֧ב יְהוָ֛ה לְבַדּ֖וֹ בַּיּ֥וֹם הַהֽוּא (oshb:Isa.2.17, byte tier), “Yahweh alone shall be exalted in that day.” (web:Isa.2.17). Verse 11, right before this row starts, is itself setumah-marked (oshb:Isa.2.11, single-witness, tier-3), the same mark disclosed as the closing witness for the stanza it ends.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the high-things catalogue (2:13-16) from its opening formula (2:12) and closing refrain (2:17) into separate rows was rejected because the catalogue is a single polysyndetic (waw-coordinated) list: the preposition עַ֥ל/וְעַ֖ל governing the quantifier כָּל as its object recurs eight times across 2:13-16, matching the governing verse's own two-part coordination at oshb:Isa.2.12 (עַ֥ל כָּל גֵּאֶ֖ה וָרָ֑ם without the conjunction, וְעַ֖ל כָּל נִשָּׂ֥א וְשָׁפֵֽל with it), not a self-standing unit, read here as enumeration inside its governing oracle rather than a separate row.

device_notes: The cedar/oak/mountain/tower/ship catalogue (2:13-16) is enumeration inside this unit, not an independent list register; polysyndetic (waw-coordinated) inventory catalogues of this kind are read as texture inside their governing oracle here, not as a unit on its own. The row's own opening seam carries undisclosed cross-seam cohesion: oshb:Isa.2.12 opens with כִּ֣י (oshb:Isa.2.12), the same particle that opens oshb:Isa.2.6 inside the preceding row's own span, both witnesses rendering it as subordinating there. The low/bow root runs unbroken across the seam and through the stanza — וַיִּשְׁפַּל (oshb:Isa.2.9), שָׁפֵ֔ל וְשַׁ֖ח (oshb:Isa.2.11), וְשָׁפֵֽל (oshb:Isa.2.12) — standing at 10 verses book-wide (sweep: 10 verses, skeleton), and it interleaves at 2:12-14 with the paired high/lofty vocabulary that the row's own catalogue enumerates (הָרָמִ֖ים וְהַנִּשָּׂאִ֑ים at oshb:Isa.2.13, הָרָמִ֑ים / הַנִּשָּׂאֽוֹת at oshb:Isa.2.14), closing again with וְשַׁח֙ גַּבְה֣וּת הָאָדָ֔ם וְשָׁפֵ֖ל at oshb:Isa.2.17. The undisclosed link leaves a live rival unstated: one sustained pride-and-humbling poem running from 2:9 through 2:17, with the refrain as internal punctuation rather than a row-cutting seam.

boundary_rationale: Opens with וְהָאֱלִילִ֖ים כָּלִ֥יל יַחֲלֹֽף (oshb:Isa.2.18, byte tier), “The idols shall utterly pass away.” (web:Isa.2.18), moving from the refrain-closed catalogue of proud things to the idols' own fate and humanity's flight into caves and holes, a fresh topical turn after the stanza-closing refrain of verse 17. The row runs through the closing exhortation “Stop trusting in man, whose breath is in his nostrils; for of what account is he?” (web:Isa.2.22), where a petuchah break is recorded (oshb:Isa.2.22, single-witness, tier-3) at the chapter's end.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading 2:18-22 as a third refrain-bounded stanza of the same shape as 2:5-11 and 2:12-17 was rejected because no closing ‘Yahweh alone… in that day’ clause recurs at its end; the unit is bounded instead by topical shift (from proud objects to idols and human flight) and the petuchah break closing the chapter.

device_notes: The ‘in that day’ temporal tag recurs at verse 20 (web:Isa.2.20), continuing the temporal frame of the refrain-closed stanzas without reopening the refrain clause itself. A flight-from-terror motif straddles the row's own opening seam: the four-token core מִפְּנֵי֙ פַּ֣חַד יְהוָ֔ה וּמֵהֲדַ֖ר recurs at oshb:Isa.2.19 and oshb:Isa.2.21 within this row, with a third site further upstream at oshb:Isa.2.10, accent_stripped tier across the three (sweep: 3 verses). Within the row, the two in-span sites share a longer eight-token run, מִפְּנֵ֞י פַּ֤חַד יְהוָה֙ וּמֵהֲדַ֣ר גְּאוֹנ֔וֹ בְּקוּמ֖וֹ לַעֲרֹ֥ץ הָאָֽרֶץ, byte-identical between oshb:Isa.2.19 and oshb:Isa.2.21 (sweep: 2 verses, byte).

boundary_rationale: Opens with the announcement formula כִּי֩ הִנֵּ֨ה הָאָד֜וֹן יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֗וֹת (oshb:Isa.3.1, byte tier), “For, behold, the Lord, Yahweh of Armies, takes away from Jerusalem and from Judah supply and support” (web:Isa.3.1), a fresh hinneh-announcement onset opening the chapter; the verse just before it, 2:22, is itself petuchah-marked (oshb:Isa.2.22, single-witness, tier-3 corroboration). The row runs through the causal explanation and the gnomic gender-reversal saying, closing on “As for my people, children are their oppressors, and women rule over them” (web:Isa.3.12), where a setumah break is recorded (oshb:Isa.3.12, single-witness, tier-3), before the fresh riv/din legal formula of verse 13.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the leadership-removal announcement (3:1-7) from the causal explanation and gnomic saying (3:8-12) into two rows was rejected because verse 8's causal ‘for’ continues explaining the same collapse announced in verse 1 without a fresh imperative, vocative, or divine-speech formula of its own; the verse-initial imperative אִמְר֥וּ (oshb:Isa.3.10) two verses later is a live rival by that same criterion, but is absorbed by the default-larger-unit rule rather than cut, since it opens no new address or addressee and continues the same gnomic-retribution texture as the surrounding verses.

device_notes: Verses 9 and 11 each carry the interjection א֣וֹי / א֖וֹי (oshb:Isa.3.9 token 10; oshb:Isa.3.11 token 1, byte tier at each site), a lexeme distinct from the hoy ה֣וֹי of oshb:Isa.1.4 and 1:24 and not blended with it here (the hoy-onset lexeme stands at 22 verses book-wide, sweep: 22 verses, skeleton); the interjection itself is a 4-verse token-exact object (sweep: 4 verses, skeleton, token-exact), while a bare three-letter substring sweep returns 8 verses, the extra 4 being contained-consonant hits inside unrelated words elsewhere in the book — these sites are read as gnomic-retribution texture inside the unit, not as fresh hoy-onset seams.

boundary_rationale: Opens with the explicit legal-summons formula נִצָּ֥ב לָרִ֖יב יְהוָ֑ה וְעֹמֵ֖ד לָדִ֥ין עַמִּֽים (oshb:Isa.3.13, byte tier), “Yahweh stands up to contend, and stands to judge the peoples.” (web:Isa.3.13), the contend-infinitive לָרִ֖יב (token 2) standing at 3 verses book-wide (sweep: 3 verses, skeleton, token-exact) and the judge-infinitive לָדִ֥ין (token 5) at exactly 1 (sweep: 1 verse, skeleton, token-exact), so the pairing cannot recur anywhere else in the book, addressed to “the elders of his people and their leaders” (web:Isa.3.14), a distinct addressee from the general my-people material of the preceding unit. The row closes on the postpositive signature נְאֻם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה צְבָאֽוֹת (oshb:Isa.3.15, byte tier), “says the Lord, Yahweh of Armies.” (web:Isa.3.15), where a setumah break is recorded (oshb:Isa.3.15, single-witness, tier-3; the verse also carries a ketiv/qere note not engaged by this quoted signature clause), before the fresh vayomer narrative onset of verse 16. This same opening seam has its own tier-3 witness: a setumah break closes verse 12 (oshb:Isa.3.12, single-witness) immediately before the row begins.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging this row into the preceding leadership-collapse unit (3:1-12) was rejected because verse 13 opens with its own verse-initial legal-summons formula, נִצָּ֥ב לָרִ֖יב יְהוָ֑ה וְעֹמֵ֖ד לָדִ֥ין עַמִּֽים (oshb:Isa.3.13, byte tier), addressed to a distinct addressee (the elders and leaders) rather than continuing the general my-people material. Running the row on to the narrative onset at oshb:Isa.3.16 was also rejected, since that verse opens its own וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֗ה narrative formula (the verse also carries a ketiv/qere note later in its own line, not engaged by this quoted onset), a distinct frame class from the postpositive neum signature closing this row at verse 15.

device_notes: unit_type trial_speech is applied here as a deviation disclosure: this row's own bytes carry the riv/din legal-summons form even though that value is more typically reserved for the book's 40-48 disputation material.

boundary_rationale: Opens with the narrative divine-speech onset וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Isa.3.16, byte tier; the verse also carries a ketiv/qere note later in its own line, not engaged by this quoted onset clause), “Moreover Yahweh said” (web:Isa.3.16), a vayomer-plus-YHWH onset distinct from the postpositive neum signature closing the preceding row, opening the judgment against the daughters of Zion. Immediately upstream of this row, verse 15 closes with a setumah break of its own (oshb:Isa.3.15, single-witness, tier-3), and a further setumah break is recorded mid-unit at the close of verse 17 (oshb:Isa.3.17, single-witness, tier-3), but the ornament catalogue of 3:18-23 is read as enumeration inside this unit rather than a separate list-register row. The row extends across the chapter division to “Seven women shall take hold of one man in that day” (web:Isa.4.1), the direct consequence of the war-deaths announced in “Your men shall fall by the sword” (web:Isa.3.25); a setumah break is recorded at the close of verse 4:1 itself (oshb:Isa.4.1, single-witness, tier-3), before the fresh in-that-day salvation turn of verse 4:2.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting the row at the 3:17|3:18 setumah break (oshb:Isa.3.17, single-witness, tier-3) into a shorter women's-judgment announcement and a separate ornament-catalogue row was rejected because the catalogue is grammatically a single finite verb's object series: יָסִ֣יר (oshb:Isa.3.18, token 3) governs, through the direct-object marker אֵ֣ת (token 5), an accumulating series of accusative objects across the catalogue, and is enumeration inside the unit, not its own literary form.

device_notes: The row deliberately crosses the chapter 3|4 division because 4:1 is the narrated outcome of the war-widowing announced within the same unit, not a fresh topic; chapter divisions are treated as tier-4 and never cut on their own authority here. The chapter-crossing itself rests on the bytes, not the rendering: oshb:Isa.4.1 opens וְהֶחֱזִיקוּ֩, a waw-prefixed perfect continuing the sequence begun at וְאָנ֥וּ וְאָבְל֖וּ (oshb:Isa.3.26, tokens 1-2), with no fresh frame, vocative, or imperative at the chapter break.

boundary_rationale: Opens with the temporal-formula turn בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא יִֽהְיֶה֙ צֶ֣מַח יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Isa.4.2, byte tier), “In that day, Yahweh's branch will be beautiful and glorious” (web:Isa.4.2), an unconditional promise sharply reversing the preceding judgment unit's mood. The row runs through the verse pairing two distinct roots in synonymous parallelism, הַנִּשְׁאָ֣ר (the book's four-way remnant-family root) and וְהַנּוֹתָר֙ (a different root, the one opening oshb:Isa.1.8) (oshb:Isa.4.3, byte tier at each), “he who is left in Zion and he who remains in Jerusalem” (web:Isa.4.3), and closes on the pavilion image “a pavilion for a shade in the daytime from the heat” (web:Isa.4.6), where a petuchah break is recorded (oshb:Isa.4.6, single-witness, tier-3) at the chapter's close. The row's own opening seam carries a mark too: a setumah break closes verse 4:1 (oshb:Isa.4.1, single-witness, tier-3) just before it.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Attaching 4:2-6 to the preceding daughters-of-Zion unit as its eventual outcome was rejected because verse 2's temporal formula introduces an unconditional promise in a wholly different register from the judgment material it follows, a sharp mode shift read as the row's own opening seam.

device_notes: The pavilion noun sukkah at the row's close, וְסֻכָּ֛ה (oshb:Isa.4.6, token 1, a vav-conjunction prefix), shares its bare consonantal root with the sukkah figure describing the besieged daughter of Zion at 1:8, כְּסֻכָּ֣ה (oshb:Isa.1.8, token 4, a kaf-preposition prefix) — as prefixed tokens the two forms collate at no tier; stripped of their prefixes the bare nouns match at accent_stripped tier, and once the noun's own homograph is excluded the object stands at exactly 2 verses book-wide (sweep: 6 verses, skeleton, of which 4 are the excluded homograph), a reversal-echo bracketing the besieged-daughter image that opens the book (1:8) and the shelter image that closes this unit (4:6), disclosed here rather than argued as a row boundary. The referent of ‘Yahweh's branch’ (web:Isa.4.2) is not decided by this row. The opening temporal formula also straddles the row's own opening seam at less than byte tier: בַּיּ֤וֹם הַהוּא֙ (oshb:Isa.4.1) stands mid-verse at tokens 6-7 against בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא (oshb:Isa.4.2) verse-initial at tokens 1-2, accent_stripped tier; the formula recurs densely nearby (sweep: 7 verses across chapters 2-4, 45 verses book-wide, skeleton) and is verse-initial at oshb:Isa.3.18 too, where it continues the same judgment material as enumeration rather than opening a seam, and what discriminates the two uses is the register shift: at 3:18 the formula introduces a further removal-item inside the same judgment oracle, while at 4:2 it introduces an unconditional salvation promise reversing that judgment mood, which is why only the latter carries the row's own opening seam.
